utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The curtains can be pulled up again. Mr. Di Fazio, yesterday we finished almost all of the session was in private session, although we finished in open session. We resume in open session. Would you please keep in mind that if there's any risk of identifying the witness that you should ask for private session. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. I'm grateful to you for that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- for that reminder, and I'll do my level best --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- and I'll try not to stray into anything that even might give away his identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Witness 6, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that was a declaration that you would speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. And apart from that, I would like to ask you whether you were able to find your orientation on the hard copy map given to you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Di Fazio, you may proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examination by Mr. Di Fazio: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you marked the map you were provided with?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness was not instructed to mark, so if he did -- have you marked the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think best would be to have it on the ELMO. And it should not be shown right away to the public. Let us look first at what we see on the map. Yes, perhaps we -- perhaps we go into the -- at least what's now on the ELMO should not be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honours, I appreciate that it's difficult to find the right orientation on the ELMO, but it appears that the markings at the bottom are not all currently in view.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They are now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And thank you, Witness, for marking those maps. Can we deal with this as easily and swiftly as we can. Firstly, did you circle the village in which you live and from which you commenced your journey?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I see circled another village which appears to be on the main road. I can't read it very clearly on the ELMO, but I think that's Vranic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you travel from your village via Vranic as you set out on this journey to visit the relatives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Having reached Vranic, did you -- tell us which way you continued.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I continued in the direction of Kline.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that on the main road that runs between Djakovica and Kline?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you assist in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- moving the map a bit in a northerly direction. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you. I'm grateful to Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have circled, it appears -- MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me for one moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've circled a village that appears to be called Rakovina. Is -- am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pass through that village or close to that village on the main road as you travelled towards your relatives' house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is on the main road, the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After going through Rakovina did you continue along the main road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you mark on this map the location at which you were stopped by the Serbian military check-point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you mark -- indicate perhaps with the marking stick the location where you were stopped by the Serbian military post.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The place is called Dolov.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And have you indicated that with a circle and some handwriting of yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were stopped at the entrance to Dolov village. The Yugoslav Army stopped me there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you have circled that on this map, is that correct, do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, having been stopped by the Serbian military check-point at this village or entrance to the village called Dolov --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I have not found it yet, but if you -- MR. DI FAZIO: On the map, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: It's called Dolovo in -- on this map which I assume is probably a -- a B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And the witness, did he not say --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's how it is written on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And this is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I found it, I found it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Where you were stopped by Yugoslav Army, yeah, that's the expression -- MR. DI FAZIO: That's how I understood his evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: -- if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you've indicated that to us on the map as well. Could you indicate to us which route you then took having been stopped by the Serbian military.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I turned back in the direction of Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as I understood your evidence from yesterday, it was on that return trip that you were stopped by the KLA soldiers; do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I turned back in the direction of Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd just like to ask you to tell the Trial Chamber of the route that you took right up until the time that you were stopped by the KLA men. Now, you've told us that you got to Dolovo. From Dolovo having been stopped, which route did you take and which villages did you pass through, if any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Dolovo, I set off in the direction of Gjakove on the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And tell us, did you continue along the road and which --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was it along that main road that you were stopped or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stopped me on the main road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you indicated on this particular map where you were stopped along the main road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you show the Judges, please, where you were stopped by the KLA soldiers along the main road. Can you indicate that using your marker.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that a marking running at right angles across the road that you have placed on the map to indicate where the KLA soldiers stopped you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's the name of that particular location, you mentioned it yesterday, I believe.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is called Ujvara or Guri i Zi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Since neither of those two locations appears as place names on the map, might the record show that the horizontal line that the witness has indicated is slightly to the north of a line running laterally through Boricic -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and on the main road. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you -- I intend -- yes, thank you. I intend to tender that map, if Your Honours please, but I ask that it remain on the ELMO for the time being as I may have to return to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P331, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If it remains on the ELMO, the ELMO should not be shown to the outside world. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. I don't know if that means, therefore, it should be taken off the ELMO now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if there's nothing else on the ELMO, I do not expect the -- MR. DI FAZIO: I can't see from here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- technicians. No, but if nothing replaces this, I do not expect the technicians to give the picture of the ELMO to the outside world if there's nothing on it. This one should at least not be shown. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to turn your mind now to events at Guri i Zi --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. If this document is going to be taken off the ELMO, I don't know whether that means that's the end of it as far as the Prosecution is concerned, or whether Mr. Di Fazio --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Di Fazio indicated that he would like to leave it on the ELMO because he might still use it --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I note there appear to be a number of other markings; I have no idea what they represent and Mr. Di Fazio may be in the same situation. MR. DI FAZIO: I am in the same situation. I think I know what they indicate and I will eventually get to that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you then. MR. DI FAZIO: But I will also seek further clarification for those extra markings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But in the meantime, Witness, I would like you to turn your mind to the point at which you were stopped at this location, Guri i Zi. You said in evidence thus far that you were stopped by KLA soldiers. Can you tell us how many approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately ten soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you recall what they were wearing and whether they were armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all armed, and they were wearing, some of them were wearing camouflage uniforms and some others were wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of them have any insignia on the uniforms or on their clothes, any patches of any sort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you asked to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They stopped me there. The road was not that good, so I was driving slowly, 10 kilometres per hour, so they took advantage of that moment to stop me and kidnap me. They checked my documents, searched me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you remain with your car and with your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for about two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that they searched you. Did they search any members of your family or your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They searched me and the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they find anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a pistol; I had an authorisation to carry it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did they locate the pistol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to the pistol? Did they leave it with you or was it seized?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They seized the pistol and all the documents I had with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you said you had to wait for two hours. Did you wait on the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We came by Drini River because it was only 200 metres away, and we stood there with my wife and children by the Drini River for two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your car moved from the road, your -- the car that you were driving, was that left on the road or was that moved as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed inside the car with my family for two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you speak to any of the KLA soldiers during that period of two hours; and if you did, can you please tell us what you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked them to release us, but they didn't. My wife recognised one of them because he was from the same part where she was coming from. But they didn't release us anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they provide you with any sort of reason as to why you had been stopped or why you were being detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said though that you waited for two hours. What happened after the two hours had elapsed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After two hours of waiting, I heard a car coming from the main road. They fired some shots. I don't know if they fired it directly into the car or in the air. They brought the car close to the location where I was. One of the soldiers asked me, "Do you recognise this car?" I said, "No". The car had Gjakove licence plates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Firstly I'd like to ask you some questions about the car. What type was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Opel Kadett make, German make. It was a light blue colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any note of the registration number? By that I mean the number plate.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except for the DJ, the first two letters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I want to ask you about any occupant of the car. Did you see anyone who was inside the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The soldier brought the car near my car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you at any time see any person that you thought was the occupant or had been the occupant of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know him. Because I had never seen that person with that car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just tell the Trial Chamber the events as they unfolded. You heard the shots fired, you've told us. You saw the Opel Kadett with the -- light blue Opel Kadett with the registration plate DJ, or part of it, DJ. And it was brought to where you were or close to where you were. From that point, how did events unfold?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20 minutes later after they had brought that car there, we set out in the direction of Jabllanice. My wife and I got on that Kadett together with a soldier, while four of our children got on my Mercedes. So we set off in the direction of some villages that I will mention later. It was a mountain path.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when you got into the Opel Kadett, did you see anything or take notice of anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was an album with photographs. I looked at those photographs and I recognised the policeman who had worked in Gjakove; he was on those photographs with his family. I knew who he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know the name or part of the name of this policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only a part of his name. I knew him as Nenad. I don't know if it was his first name or last name; I only knew him as Nenad. I knew where he was from. He was from Kline municipality, Binxh village. He worked as a policeman in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what ethnicity was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he was a Serb or Montenegrin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, up until this point, up until this point, the point which you got into the car and saw the album, the photo album, and saw this man's photographs, had you actually laid eyes on him up until that point or had you not seen him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had seen him before, when he worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understood that, but what I'm asking about is at the -- on this day. Up until the point when you got into the car and you saw the photo album, had you actually laid eyes on the driver of the Kadett, the Opel Kadett?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you started to tell us of the drive that you then embarked on from the point at which you were stopped. You've told us that you were in the Kadett with your wife and one of your children and the other kids were in the other car, your own car. I want you to tell us -- I want you to tell us which route you took and where you ended up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got on the main road in the direction of Gjakove. There is a place called Mrasor, it's on the map, and there, there is a bridge. We entered the village of Kralan. We spent a few minutes in the car there, at that location. From Kralan, we proceeded in the direction of Bishtrica e Decanit and then to Kpuz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you indicated these places on the map that you took home with you last night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can we place the map on the ELMO, and if necessary, Your Honours, I'd like the ELMO not to -- if Your Honour -- I don't think this will have any effect of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we limit ourselves to the portion of the ELMO not marked, not the southern part. I'd prefer to have it not on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think -- I think that may not achieve the objective that Your Honour has in mind, given the testimony that I anticipate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then what is now on the ELMO should not be shown to the public. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you. All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you would, please, indicate with the marker pen the villages that you passed through on your -- on your trip in the Opel Kadett.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Opel Kadett. Here is Mrasor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And from there ...?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We passed the bridge over Drini River and arrived in Kralan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you pass through Kralan or did anything in particular happen there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you, sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you -- did your vehicle, the Opel Kadett, simply drive through the village and continue on its way or did you stop and do anything there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we passed through that village. We continued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Keep going in your narrative and tell us the route that you took and the villages, just as you have been doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we move the map down a little so that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is where Kralan is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, a little bit further up now. Yes. Thank you, we have Kralan visible now. MR. DI FAZIO: I think, as Mr. Emmerson suggested, a little further down might be helpful.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Kralan is here. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just so we can all see what's on the map it needs to come down the screen where all of the markings trace the route of the journey. So if Kralan can come down the screen a little bit further and then some more, I think we then have the image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Overall view. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And please, Witness, continue as you have been describing this journey.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So here is Kralan. You can see my arrow here we crossed Bishtrica e Decanit and up here is Kpuz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you pass through Kpuz and continue on your way?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And continue your narrative as before. I'd like to know if you just drove through Gllogjan or whether you stopped there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The direction of our movement with the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Sorry to rise, but I think we're going to need a redaction at 16, line 7, the village that is named there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've been thinking about it. I'll consider it with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I -- sorry, may I make one observation. I think because we went into private session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I understand what the reason is, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although the evidence elicited in private session was -- contained some more details.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't think there's any need for redaction in respect of the part in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll instruct Madam Registrar to the extent. Rather too much than ... Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours, and if Your Honours please that -- I believe that the map has now been given ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I believe the map has now been given an exhibit number. I have no further need to use it with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since you intend to tender it -- MR. DI FAZIO: I did. I thought it had been given a number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you tender it and then I ask if there's any objections. MR. DI FAZIO: I formally tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, might I actually see the original because it's a little hard to make out on the ELMO and I'd just like to have a look before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Absolutely, no problem, and may I see it myself, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, since Mr. Harvey asked first, to give the original of the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that we with can continue while looking at these maps of like on -- looking at this map. Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Yes we can. Just give me a -- if Your Honours would be so kind as to bear with me for a moment. Yeah. Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before we get on to events in Jablanica, you've told us of this trip in detail and that you were in the Opel Kadett. As far as you're aware, was your car, your own vehicle, travelling with you, as you made this trip to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was following the Opel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you -- were you aware of any other cars or was it, as far as you're aware, a two-car convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were only two cars. I did not see any other cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever see any other persons other than KLA soldiers and/or your own family members in either of those two cars or is that all that -- were they the only people who were in the cars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only these two people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it when you say, "only these two people," you mean only these two groups of people, the KLA soldiers and/or -- and your family members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, two cars, two people from the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand you. Now, you said that you arrived at Jablanica. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what -- where you were taken once you arrived in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took me to a room close to the entrance to the courtyard. I can show you later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, do your best, if you can, to try and describe the building that you were taken to and where this place was in Jablanica, as best you can and from what your memory tells you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning when they took me in through the gate, I was not left there for long. Then they took me to a house with red bricks. It had four rooms and it was in the middle of the courtyard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Single-storey? Double-storey?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you something on the television screen that you can see there. MR. DI FAZIO: And I'd like to have produced to the witness, please, what I believe is 65 ter 1103.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting, Mr. Harvey, you wanted to see the map first before you expressed whether you had any objections against --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, then no objections against. P331 is admitted under seal. Witness 6, it takes a while until it appears on the screen, but it will be there soon. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at that image; can you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's obviously in a ruined condition now, but -- well, firstly, do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where I stayed for six weeks as a prisoner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moments ago in your testimony, you said that you were taken to a building and you were taken through a courtyard and into a building which had four rooms. Is that the same building that you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the one with the four rooms, the one that I see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you were there, was it in this condition or was it better maintained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in better shape that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you look in the photograph you will obviously see a gentleman kneeling down looking into what appear to be two holes. Do you know what is underneath the house and what the gentleman might be looking at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a basement there. There's water in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see that basement in your time at Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two weeks before I was released, when I had a little bit more freedom, I could see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If Your Honours please, I tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P332, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, I take it from the three times nodding no. P332 is admitted into evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: I -- yes. Thank you. I want to show the witness a second photograph. This one does not have ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me so I may consult with my case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: While that's being done, I can move on briefly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were there for six weeks. How long did you actually stay in that place that you've just indicated to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Six weeks, all the time, maybe two days less than six weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you recall the date when you left Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 25th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of which month, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: July, the seventh month, July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like you to return now to your arrival, your first arrival, at this particular location. You've told us about the house now, and we're talking about the day when you first arrived and when you were first brought there. You said that you were taken in, into the house, and I want you now to tell the Trial Chamber what happened to you once you were taken into the house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I asked first to see another photograph of the first room where I was taken to, and there's the place where I was beaten by the soldiers. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll show you some -- do I understand, Witness, that you were saying that in the photograph that was shown to you, you can see the room where you were first beaten; do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I should have -- I didn't realise that. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness please be shown --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not this photograph that you showed me just now, the other one. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll show you another photograph in a while. Don't worry about that. But in the meantime, let's just come back now to the events that occurred to you. You said that you were beaten. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what happened to you and how it started and how it developed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was beaten until they were exhausted. The soldiers beat me up one after the other, sometimes with a baseball bat and sometimes with other things, whatever they could lay their hands on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's get to some more detail about this, please. Firstly, you say "the soldiers"; what soldiers were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA soldiers that pretended they were fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these soldiers who had brought you in the car, in the Opel Kadett and your own car, or were they other soldiers who were already there, or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'll ask you about that perhaps later, but at this time I want you to focus -- I want you to focus now on the first day that you were there. At this time did you know any of the soldiers who were beating you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you stayed there for a period of six weeks. Did you come to know any of the soldiers who were in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The names of the people who tortured me are written down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They may be written down, but I want to hear them from you. I want to hear them from your own mouth, please, if you know of any.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Lahi Brahimaj, with his brother Nazmi, his cousin Hamza, these were the initiators of my beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Firstly, Lahi Brahimaj, did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Maxhupi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Nazmi Brahimaj, did he have a nickname or did you just know him as Nazmi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't. He did not have a nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the man Hamza, did he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what Hamza's surname or family name was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew his name, but I learned his surname much later, it's Brahimaj, because I wanted to know. I knew all three of them by appearance because they were close to me all the time, non-stop, when they beat me and tortured me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, you've given us the names of some of the people who you say tortured you, but now turn your mind back again. I must ask you to turn your mind back again to this first beating that you've started to describe, the one that happened to you when you first arrived in Jablanica on that day. And what I'd like you to tell the Trial Chamber is this: Can you tell us if any of those individuals whom you have named participated in beating you that first day that you arrived in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which of them participated in beating you on that first day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nazmi.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How long did the beating last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how long it lasted because I lost consciousness during the beating; I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were instruments used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A baseball bat. I was punched. Anything they could use they did against me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They used their feet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was beaten on my legs, arms, I have fractures on my body, I had bruises on my back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, remember, we're focusing -- we're focusing on the first day, remember that, when you first arrived. During that occasion, were you ever offered -- were you ever told in any way at all as far as you could ascertain why this was happening to you, what the reason was for this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've mentioned the man whom you saw photographs of in the Opel Kadett, a man you knew as Nenad. Did you ever see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in the same room together that night, both of us were beaten. We were tied up with a rope. We were, both of us, tied up for 24 hours, until the next day in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you actually see, yourself, with your own eyes Nenad being beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've given the Trial Chamber an idea of the type of beating that you suffered. Did Nenad also suffer that sort of beating, same force, instruments, kicking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know who participated in the beating of Nenad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nazmi, with a group of soldiers that they came. The soldiers were not always the same ones. They took turns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did Nenad stay there in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the next day in the afternoon. He stayed there for 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did he depart his room in Jablanica? How did he go? How did he leave it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Two soldiers came and took him with them, and I don't know what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of condition was he in when the two soldiers came and took him? Can you tell us if he was -- let me be more specific with you. Can you tell the Trial Chamber: A, if he was walking; if he had any visible signs of blood or any other visible injuries on him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had everything you mentioned on him. He wasn't able to walk. Both of us, actually, did have the same injuries. We were both beaten up. These two soldiers took him, and I don't know what they did with him afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Nenad again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that they were beating Nenad, did you ever hear of anything from the soldiers that shed any light on why he was being beaten, why he was being attacked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'd just like to now return to the photographs, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, Mr. Di Fazio, for purely logistical reasons, I would like to have a rough idea on how much time you would need, and then to hear from the other parties as well, just to see whether there's any chance that the next witness would be called today because -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, my estimation is that there is virtually no chance of the other witness being called today. I have -- I think you will gather, a number of other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you would say -- if you would tell me how much time you would need, then we could hear from the Defence, approximately. MR. DI FAZIO: I would need at least another two hours, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Another two hours. Then I take it for granted that there's no chance that the next witness would be called today.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: None whatsoever, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, this information can be passed. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd just like to return briefly to the photographs. There's one more photograph I'd like to show you, if I may. Could you -- MR. DI FAZIO: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit -- sorry, 65 ter 1357, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise that building and that -- in that landscape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the gate to the yard where you see some holes here, some windows, there was a room there, that's where myself and Nenad spent the night. And then we moved to the other building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What other building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one you can see here, the one that you showed me earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the six-week period that you were in Jablanica, did you stay in the one building? Did you stay there at nights at least?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that building that you see in that photograph in front of you the building where you stayed for six weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one with the roof which is not destroyed is the one where I stayed the rest of the time, while this part here which looks like burned, this is where I spent the first night with Nenad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be able to simply mark that photograph. The usher will help you and give you a pen. If you would just mark, perhaps put a circle, a circle around the window of the room, carefully put a circle around the window of the room where you and Nenad were -- were beaten.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please assist the witness in marking so that he knows how to do it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The whole area here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we get rid of the marking as it is now, and then, Mr. Di Fazio, if you clearly ask the witness what exactly to mark, and then Madam Usher will assist him in marking. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you've told us that you were beaten when you first arrived in Jablanica and that it happened in a building, along with Nenad. Can you indicate the room on any structure that you see there where you were beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first night, this part here is close to the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a building there in existence when you arrived that is not there in the photograph now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was covered. For 20 metres it was entirely covered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that both parties have looked at these photographs, and the picture, for someone who sees it for the first time, the -- well, let's say the middle lower part could be either a wall with white parts in it, or it could be two walls, three openings on the left, giving a view on an internal wall which is white. If the parties could agree on whether this is not just a wall, but a surface, two walls, one with three openings giving view on a white internal wall, which we also see in the middle where it seems that there's a larger opening, then I'd like to know because then we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, having been there myself and having looked at the site, I can confirm that the red brick through which you can see the grey/white wall behind is, in fact, a building obviously in a very badly destroyed state at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: But that is a grey wall bordering the road that you can see behind it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are looking at a red brick wall and another wall behind it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps a roof may have been up there earlier. Mr. Di Fazio, would you agree because the picture as such -- MR. DI FAZIO: Is deceiving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it needs some interpretation -- MR. DI FAZIO: It needs some interpretation, yes, because it's not immediately clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the -- you've circled the building or the room in which you were beaten with Nenad. Do I understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there's another building on the right-hand side of the photograph, you can see it, it's still got a roof, although that's ruined. Did you spend any time in that building as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this other building here?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The one on the right, it's got a roof, it's still got a roof --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We spent one night where the white wall is seen here. It's on the side of the road, while the red bricks are on the side of the yard. We spent the first night there, and then both me and Nenad were moved to this other building which had four rooms. I was in the room which was on the left side as you enter the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me this: Is that -- is that room that you've just mentioned in the structure with the remains of a roof on it, was that where you spent most of your time in Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it have a window?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on that side facing the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the window in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I seek to tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P332, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that there are no objections, then this marked photograph is admitted into evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Is it 332, Your Honours, or 333?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the previous photograph was -- MR. DI FAZIO: 332.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- 33 -- let me -- Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. This will be Exhibit Number P333.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then P333 is admitted into evidence. I thank you for -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions about the people whose names you've mentioned. In the six weeks that you were in Jablanica, did you see KLA soldiers every day or infrequently? Can you tell us how often you saw them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was locked except for the last two weeks when I had more freedom to move. During the time when I was locked, I didn't see any except for those who were brought there to beat and torture me. And to tell you the truth, you cannot count them, they were numerous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So -- so approximately the first four weeks you were literally imprisoned in a room, do I -- or at least in a house. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you guarded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. When the door was closed I couldn't see if there was a guard or not standing on the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you joined at any time by any other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For quite some time, I was all alone. After two or so weeks, they brought three other persons in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to ask you questions about the other people who joined you later, but I now want to turn back to the KLA people. You only saw them when they arrived. Were you beaten always when the KLA soldiers were there or did it not happen -- did it not work out that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I was always beaten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the names of some of the KLA men you say you saw there, and you've mentioned Lahi Brahimaj, Nazmi Brahimaj, and Hamza. How did you find out their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I was released, I wanted to find out their names. I knew them by appearance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ever introduce themselves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to focus on them as individuals now. Let's start with Lahi Brahimaj. How often would you say you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Continuously. I saw him there continuously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the Trial Chamber would like to know -- would like a bit for exactitude, I think. You try and do your best. They couldn't have been there constantly for four weeks, so you tell the Trial Chamber how often you saw them. Once a day? Once a week? Twice a day? Three times a week? Try and give us that sort of detail.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, two days would not pass without seeing Lahi Brahimaj there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that he had a nickname, Maxhupi. How did you come to discover that nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a cousin of his who worked there as a cook, so when I discussed with him -- when we had casual conversations, I asked him about the other person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get to that period of time when you were a cook later. But turn your mind to the other man you call Hamza. I want to know the same information there. How often did you see him in that four-week period? I'm talking about the four-week period, your initial four-week period.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost every day, because their house was nearby the place where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that the house was nearby to the place where they were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked Gani Brahimaj, the cook. I was interested to find out these details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And Nazmi Brahimaj, in that four-week period, how often did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nazmi was there all the time, maybe a day would pass without seeing him, but he was there continuously. He moved about that place all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When these three men came to your room in that four-week period, how long would you be with them on each occasion? I assume it varied, but can you give us an idea of a range of time, how long you were with each of them. In other words, did they come for an hour or two or five minutes or the whole day? Give us an idea of how long you would have had them in sight.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the prisoners or the other? Could you please explain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. I've been asking you about Lahi Brahimaj, Nazmi Brahimaj, and the man Hamza. Now, when you were a prisoner and you said they came to your room, to the room in which you were kept, how long would they stay in the room? Was it a short period of time? A long period of time? Did it vary? Please tell the Trial Judges and give them an idea.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would come for five minutes, ten minutes, whenever they wanted and stayed as long as they wanted, but usually this long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they do when they came to your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They beat me with baseball bats, with fists. For two weeks, I didn't know much of myself, I didn't know where my face was, where my neck was. I was all swollen up because of the beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Other than baseball bats, were any other instruments used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ever arrive - and I'm talking about the three men: Lahi Brahimaj, Nazmi Brahimaj, and Hamza - did they ever arrive and not beat you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such occasions, but rarely this happened because they would send other soldiers to beat me up. It wasn't necessary that they themselves beat me up when they had others to send over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When other soldiers beat you up, were they present or had they sent them? I want to know if they were actually in the room seeing what was happening when other soldiers beat you up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These three would leave the room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I need to know a bit more detail about this type of beating that you've just described. You said that there were occasions when other soldiers beat you up. You just said these three, and you're talking, I understand, about Lahi Brahimaj, Nazmi Brahimaj, and Hamza. You said that they would leave the room. Were they ever in the room at the same time as the other soldiers who were beating you up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Nazmi was there in the room. Sometimes Lahi would happen to be there in the room. Not all the three of them came at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What about facilities in the room? Can you tell us if you had any facilities, anything like a bed or blankets, anything -- any furniture, anything at all inside the room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my stay there for the first three weeks, there was nothing in the room, only the floor. No covering, no blankets, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm going to move on to the topic of other people, and this would be a natural break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be better to have a break. We'll have a break for 25 minutes. We'll resume at ten minutes past 4.00, but I add to that sometimes, often for good reasons, the Chamber is late. The Chamber, however, also very often has to wait until whoever in this courtroom is ready, whether technicians or counsel or -- the Chamber would like to get started in time, and therefore urges everyone to be here at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Di Fazio, and Witness 6, there are a few procedural matters I'd like to deal with without further delay. So if you would forgive us for not immediately continuing your examination. Mr. Di Fazio, the Chamber was informed that the two applications for subpoenas filed yesterday and today, one in relation to a witness number 55 in the tentative order of testimony and the other one about Witness 18, that the Office of the Prosecution would like to make an oral application to change the dates to appear in the subpoenas, thus that Witness number 55 in the tentative order of testimony would be subpoenaed for the 20th of June and not for the 14th. MR. DI FAZIO: I understood, if Your Honours please, the 21st.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 21. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have on my list for Witness 18 -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- The 21st and not the 15th -- MR. DI FAZIO: I had the 20th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like to be sure because I'm about to ask the -- first of all, is there -- usually subpoenas, unless there's a specific cry for submissions, we deal with them. Could the Defence perhaps please verify whether there are any problems similar to the ones raised the day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't have notice of the two witnesses that Your Honour was going to raise at this stage. I can't imagine that there are, but I will check, if I may, and verify that there are no concerns. But they're not going to be concerns about the date in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I do understand that. The reason why I'm urging the parties so much is that the time reserved for calling the witnesses and everything that's needed, passports, visa, et cetera, might be relatively short. And therefore, if we could deal with it today, if I could sign decisions today, I would certainly try to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've been able to identify as Your Honour has been speaking who it is that these subpoenas relate to, and I have no observations to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: None to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Nor I, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Di Fazio, it certainly becomes important because on the basis of the information provided of course by the OTP itself, drafts have been made for subpoenas on the dates indicated, and I am, in view of the fact that there are no objections, I'm ready to sign but I'd rather not sign subpoenas with the wrong dates on it. MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours, what I suggest is this: This is a matter that we can quickly -- we've obviously got the dates right, it's just the information that I have may be that I'm applying the wrong date to one of the witnesses. Can I suggest we just move on and I'll be able to instantly provide the information to you perhaps at the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, filing decisions usually goes until 4.00. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, there are a few possibilities. One is that the Chamber staff made mistakes in writing down the suggested dates. There's another possibility that the OTP changed its mind since then. If it would be the second, we are trying to deliver decisions as quickly as we can in relatively late applications for subpoenas. Of course, if the mistake is at the Chamber's staff side, then it is the Chamber, not the staff, but the Chamber that takes responsibility; if not, however, I'd like you to verify that immediately. MR. DI FAZIO: I can let -- I can let the Trial Chamber know within, I would say, a matter of a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll -- then I'm not going to sign at this moment. The staff is ready -- if finally the dates are wrong, and if for Witness 25, it should be 21st and then witness 18, it would then be 20th. MR. DI FAZIO: The dates are completely correct is my information; it's only which witness that the dates apply to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but nevertheless it's important for a witness who is subpoena to know which dates is his, isn't it? MR. DI FAZIO: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, either it is as I said before, that's Witness 55 for the 20th and Witness 18 for the 21st or the other way around. I'll instruct my staff to make alternative drafts changing the dates so that upon your -- upon receiving the information about which date for which witness, I can immediately sign one of the versions of the subpoena. Having clarified this, we'll wait for your information. There is another matter. I think on the 22nd of May the Trial Chamber has provisionally admitted, under seal I think, at least for two out of three witnesses 92 bis statements, that is, for witnesses without cross-examination. Why were they -- no. The issue was, as a matter of fact, that two of these witnesses, we are now informed, do not require protective measures. A third one, there's an application pending for protective measures. The OTP was requested to inform the Trial Chamber about security and safety status. You've done so, but the statements have not yet been uploaded in e-court. And therefore in order to be -- numbers to be assigned, you are invited to upload them, if the attestations still are needed then we'd like to be informed about that as well. But at least they have not been uploaded yet and I ask the attention of the Prosecution for that. Then -- yes. We also understand that the Office of the Prosecution has now prepared clean copies of eight exhibits attached to the Limaj transcript of witness Jakup Krasniqi. Numbers still should be assigned to them. I say eight because there were originally nine, but number 5 was the same as number 12 attached to the witness statement of the same -- of the same witness. Therefore, the eight now clean copies, that is, without P numbers from the Limaj case, should be assigned numbers. If you could provide -- I don't know whether you've uploaded them already in e-court. MR. DI FAZIO: I believe they have been done. I was informed that that has occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then, Madam Registrar, I take it on the basis of the list you received earlier that you already assigned numbers to it in the e-court system and that once you've done that the parties will be informed about which these numbers are. If I remember well, there were no objections to any of these documents attached to the Limaj transcript. Having dealt with these matters, we can now continue. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. Would Your Honours just give me one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to return now to the personalities at -- that you saw at Jablanica. You've mentioned the names of three individuals who beat you, KLA soldiers. Did you, beyond those three names, Lahi Brahimaj, Nazmi Brahimaj, and Hamza, did you come to know the names of any other KLA soldiers at Jablanica during your time there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard these names in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You -- earlier in your testimony you mentioned other people coming into the room, other non-KLA soldiers. Were you joined at any time by other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall who was the first or who joined you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he alone or with others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three others, Montenegrins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they arrive all at once or were they brought separately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how long had you been there at the time that these -- this group arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had been there for about four weeks or three and a half weeks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know or did you ascertain any details about the Bosnian, first of all? Did you find out his name; if not, did you know anything about him or find out anything about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know his name, but I could hear the soldiers saying, the Bosnian, he was a Muslim, he had been working in Decani in Elektrokosova company and he spoke a little Albanian with me. The other three, the Montenegrins, they did not speak to me and I don't know their names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you give us a description of the Montenegrins who were with you, at least their ages if possible and, if you can recall, the clothing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosnian had light trousers, light shirt, summer shirt, dark colour. The Montenegrins, one of them was older than the others and he had a jacket on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the -- of the Montenegrins, was there -- could you tell if one was markedly younger than the others or all that you could tell was that one was older than the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 35 years old or 40 years old, I mean the older one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long were the Montenegrins and the Bosnian with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About three days. They were in the room that I was for three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to them in the three days that they were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were beaten, just like I was beaten in the beginning, and I was beaten during the three days that they stayed there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were instruments used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of instruments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Baseball bat, and they also stabbed them with knives. Their clothes were full of blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's -- give the Trial Chamber a clearer idea of this process of them being stabbed with knives. I want to know exactly how that works -- how that happened. Were they stabbed severely? Not so severely? More than once? Explain it more carefully, please, to the Trial Chamber, this process of the use of the knife.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you. They were pricked with knives on -- all over their bodies, about one centimetre deep, the three of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that caused bleeding, I take it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were bleeding as a result of these knife pricks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were bleeding, and because of the beating they also spat blood. They were covered in blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that the Montenegrin -- that the -- the Montenegrins and the Bosniak were in the room, did you see any of the other personalities whose names you've mentioned, Lahi Brahimaj, Nazmi Brahimaj, and Hamza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nazmi and Hamza were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the room, the inside of the room in which you and these men were incarcerated look like? Did it have anything on the walls?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing. Just a wooden floor. The room was 4 metres by 4, not bigger than that. They stayed there for three days, and I did not see them after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there blood on the walls?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that -- it's too late to object to what is an obvious leading question, but it looks as if he's got the wrong answer anyway.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Um -- MR. DI FAZIO: Well, with respect, I don't think it is. The witness has said that these men were cut and pricked all over their bodies. One -- and I think he said that they were bleeding and they were beaten and they were spitting blood. In those circumstances, it's hardly leading, I think, to ask if there was blood on the walls. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, there could be no leading on whether there was blood. Leading was whether it was on the walls, the ceiling, or the floor. I would not disallow such a question, as a matter of fact. So -- MR. DI FAZIO: I can rephrase it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any blood in that room, other than on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: The question has already been asked and answered, effectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The answer is -- well, the -- the transcript is not clear in that respect, Mr. Harvey, because the answer comes after your objection in the transcript, whether that fully reflects what happened is a different matter. That's the reason why I allow Mr. Di Fazio to put the question again to the witness, and then hear the answer. Because your objection suggests that the question had already been answered and in accordance with the transcript it had not yet been. So therefore, that creates some confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I heard, of course, the answer while I was on my feet objecting, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that I didn't hear it. Mr. Di Fazio, you may put the question to the witness again. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll try and put it in as neutral a way as I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than on the men, did you see blood anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was blood on the floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the time that these men were in the room there with you, did you ever hear anything that explained why they were there? Did you ever get any information about that topic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't speak to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, who took them away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was late when they took them. It was about 10.00 p.m. when they took them away, and after that I don't know what happened to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see them again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After they had departed, did you see anyone else in your room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- tell us who -- what happened in that respect, how another person came to be there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two weeks before I was released, as I said, I had more freedom and I saw when they brought three other persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they brought all at once or did they come at different times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At different times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can -- it's been a long time, but please do the best you can. Can you try and give us a sequence of who arrived and a description of that person, if you can. Who was the first to arrive? And we're now talking about the period of time after the Montenegrins and the Bosnian had left. Who was the first to arrive after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. An Albanian, a Muslim, from Zahaq of Peje. They brought him in the boot of the car. I saw him because I was outside, so he was in the boot of the car. They beat him the same as they did me and tortured him until he died.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember the make of car that he was brought in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. It was a Mercedes 190, metallic colour, 190.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long was that individual there with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/6 [Resumed]
